title: Golem provisional (spike-dependent) definitions
description: Every data shape whose final form depends on the Phase 3 Mineflayer feasibility spike (decision point D3). Isolated here so a D3 change touches this file and SPIKE_DEPENDENCIES.md, plus the few refs listed there. Each definition names the SPIKE_DEPENDENCIES.md item (S-n) it belongs to. No spike report existed when these were drafted (docs/spike/ is absent), so every default is the readiness review's suggested default.

KeyCause.description: S-2, §14.5 attribution of one key change: {"own": actionId} when the change is an expected effect of a live action of this bot, else "outside". Provisional rule (review question 4 default): Own exactly when the key is in the action's affected-key set and the change arrives between start and the action's verdict plus the settle window max(4t, 2 x round-trip time); changes caused by cancelled or rolled-back actions are Outside.

RoundTripTime.description: S-2, §17.1 settle window input: the latest round-trip time in milliseconds as the backend measured it (keep-alive or ping), or null before the first measurement. Recorded in TickInput so that a runtime-side settle or attribution computation replays exactly (§15.5).

FlushMode.description: S-1, finding 3: when the backend's packets for an action leave. "deferred": start() only queues, flush() in phase 7 sends (§15.2 as written). "immediate": packets leave during start() or cancel() in phase 6 and flush() sends what remains. Determinism is defined at the ingest boundary in both modes (§15.5), so either is conforming if D3 confirms that; the runtime only logs the mode.

BackendCapabilities.description: S-1, S-2: what the connected backend guarantees, returned by connect() (backend-data.schema.json ConnectResult).

attribution.description: S-2: "backend" when the backend tags every change Own or Outside (§14.5 as written); "affected-keys" is reserved for a no-go outcome in which the runtime attributes from Delta affected-key sets instead.

VersionDataSources.description: S-3, question 5: where the runtime loads version data for the pinned Minecraft version. Provisional default: the vanilla data generator for registries, block states, tags and recipes (§18.1); minecraft-data for hardness, outline and collision shapes, burn times and tool tiers; a hand-authored placement table for can_place and place_state (decisions 68, 87).

registries.description: Directory produced by java -DbundlerMainClass=net.minecraft.data.Main -jar server.jar --all, cached per version.

physics.description: Package and data version supplying hardness, shapes, burn times and tool tiers.

placement.description: Hand-authored placement-rule table with an explicit v0.1 scope (review finding 4).
